artifacts.summary: Six-phase implementation closing the plan-to-file_scope reconciliation gap: a deployed-tree refusal at the harvester, deposit site, and containment site (PART A), advisory authoring-shape detection at plan acceptance, and a mechanical follow-up-commit trigger plus a read-only annotation lookup for within-dispatch drops (PART B). Records a significant, well-justified deviation from the plan's literal union design for Phase 4, and two recorded Site-3 residuals for a future task.

completion_data.completion_summary: Closed the plan-to-file_scope reconciliation gap across six phases: a deployed-tree refusal enforced at the harvester, the proposed_file_scope deposit site, and git-commit-phase.sh's own Containment Self-Check (closing a live loophole where a bare .claude/ entry admitted every deployed-tree path), advisory authoring-shape detection in validate-artifact.sh, and a mechanical follow-up-commit trigger in the implementing agent's own protocol. Phase 4's planned admitting union was built, found to regress a pre-existing idempotence fixture via git-commit-scoped.sh's separate, un-patched Site-3 containment guard, and replaced with a read-only annotation lookup instead -- recorded as a deviation with full reasoning. All ten edited source-store files redeployed and verified byte-identical; 196 fixture-suite assertions across four extended test suites, all green.

memory_candidates.content: When a decision admits a path/value at one of several independent checking sites that all consult the same underlying declared state (here: git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check vs. git-commit-scoped.sh's separate V10 guard, both reading specs/state.json's file_scope), admitting it at only one site can create either a false success (the other site silently vetoes it downstream) or a regression in an existing fixture that depended on the old, consistently-rejecting behavior. Before implementing a 'make X admit this' fix, trace the decision through every other site that independently re-checks the same state, or build a small reproduction against the real pipeline before committing to the design -- a design that looks correct in isolation can still fail once the full call chain is exercised.

A repo-wide lint that pattern-matches on 'mentions script X's literal filename AND contains a pipe character on the same line' (to catch piped phase-commit invocations hiding an exit code) will false-positive on a test fixture's own grep pattern string that happens to name the script inside a quoted literal (e.g. `echo "$out" | grep -q "git-commit-phase.sh: ..."`). Fix by rephrasing the grep pattern to a narrower substring that still distinguishes the intended message from a sibling script's differently-worded one (e.g. match on the message's distinguishing WARNING-prefix/colon shape rather than the script's own filename), rather than suppressing or allowlisting the whole file.

A single structural-prefix regex `^\.claude(/.*)?$` cleanly and correctly covers all three shapes of a deployed-tree path claim in one test: the bare directory name (`.claude`), the trailing-slash form (`.claude/`), and any nested path under it (`.claude/foo/bar.sh`) -- because the optional group `(/.*)?` matches both an empty continuation (the bare/trailing-slash forms, since `.*` matches zero characters) and any nested path. Reusable whenever a 'this whole subtree, however it's spelled' refusal/match is needed against a declared path list.
